transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up time from someone who needs it more, but... well, I suppose I just haven't been feeling quite right lately. It's nothing terrible, really, just... I've started to feel, in a rather quiet but stubborn way, that maybe the best version of my life is behind me. I keep trying to stay disciplined and plan my days, but it just feels like no amount of effort is going to get me back to feeling like myself. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it alright.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, I suppose... I hope I don't sound like I'm just complaining about getting older, but it's been quite a while now. I'd say it really started after a hiking injury I had. That was a little over three years ago—about three years and three months now, if I'm being precise. I tried not to make a big fuss about it at the time, you know, just pushing through so I wouldn't be a bother to anyone, but that seems to be when this sort of... quiet slump really settled in. Is that the sort of detail you were looking for?
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, don't bring you the same pleasure they used to?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I've lost all pleasure. I certainly don't want to give the impression that I'm just sitting around moping all day. I still try to keep busy, you know? I read my history books, and I make sure to attend my weekly coffee group with the old colleagues. 

I suppose... well, maybe it's just that I don't get quite as excited about them as I used to. It's more of a routine now, something I do because I know I should, rather than something I'm really looking forward to. But I still do them! I'm trying my best to stay active and engaged. I hope that's not too unusual for someone my age?
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or like you're not living up to who you feel you should be, especially lately?

Oh, well... no, I don't think so. I certainly hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself! I try very hard to keep up with my responsibilities, you know, keeping the house in order and making sure I'm not a burden to my children or anyone else. 

I suppose my role has changed a bit since I retired, but... no, I wouldn't say I feel guilty or like I'm letting anyone down. I really do try to do the best I can every day with what I have. I hope that's an alright answer? I just haven't really noticed that particular feeling, to be honest.

Have you been having any trouble with your sleep lately, such as difficulty falling asleep, waking up frequently during the night, or waking up earlier than you'd like and not being able to go back to sleep?

Well, I... I think my sleep is mostly fine. I mean, at my age, you don't really expect to sleep like a teenager anymore, do you? I usually manage to get some rest. 

I don't want to sound like I'm complaining about every little ache and pain, but... well, I suppose I do wake up sometimes during the night. Not all the time, just... occasionally. But I usually just read a book for a bit, or get up and have a glass of water, and try not to disturb anyone. I'm sure that's fairly typical, isn't it? I just try to make the best of it and get back to sleep when I can. I hope that's the kind of information you need?
Have you noticed feeling more tired than usual, even after getting enough rest, or found that even small tasks take a lot more effort than they used to?

Well, I... I definitely try to keep my energy up. I don't want you to think I'm just lying in bed all day! I still get up every morning, I do the shopping, and I tinker with some of my little projects around the house. I make a point of it.

But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest... I have noticed that things take a bit more out of me lately. Even small things, like setting up for a mentoring session I do with some younger folks, or just walking through a community event... they leave me feeling quite worn out. And it's a sort of tiredness that a nap doesn't really seem to fix, you know? But I still push through and get things done! I just... I hope it's not too much of a bother that I'm slowing down a little bit. That's to be expected, right?
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or remember things lately?

Well, I... I don't think so, no. I mean, my memory is still quite sharp, thankfully! I don't want you to think I'm getting forgetful or anything like that. I still manage all my own finances and keep track of all my appointments without any trouble. 

I suppose sometimes I might take a little longer to decide what to have for dinner, or maybe I'll misplace my reading glasses for a moment, but... well, that happens to everyone, doesn't it? Especially at my age. I always find them eventually! I really try to stay on top of things and keep my mind active. I hope that's what you were looking for? I haven't really noticed any real problems with my focus or anything.
Would you say that you’ve stopped doing or participating in things you used to care about or look forward to, even if you still do them occasionally?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I've stopped doing things completely. I mean, I still keep the house in order, and I make sure I manage the day-to-day basics just fine. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just letting everything go! 

But... I suppose, if I think about it... my weeks are a bit, well, smaller than they used to be. I've sort of... stepped back a little from some things. Like the mentoring I mentioned, and some of the community events... even the music gatherings I used to enjoy so much. And I haven't really made any travel plans lately. I just... I suppose I don't quite have the same drive for them right now. But I still do the important things! I hope it's okay that I've quieted down my schedule a bit? I just thought maybe it was time to take things a little easier.
Would you say that some of the things you used to really enjoy, like the music gatherings or mentoring, feel more like chores now than something you look forward to?

Oh, no, I wouldn't call them chores! I don't want you to think I'm ungrateful for those opportunities or that I resent the people involved. They're wonderful people, they really are. 

I suppose... well, maybe I don't get quite that same... spark of excitement when I think about going. It's more that I just feel a bit... settled, I guess? Like I've done my part and it's okay to let others take the lead. But when I do go, I still try to be pleasant and helpful. I always put on a smile and make sure everyone else is having a good time. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? I just wouldn't want anyone to feel like I was dragging my feet.
